AbsolutizeUrlOp.description: Resolves the value against the page's base URL (RFC 3986 §5).
AbsolutizeUrlOp.title: AbsolutizeUrlOp

ActionsReport.description:
What a listing's browser actions did: the mechanism that grew the list (None when none did), why they stopped,
the actions taken, the document states kept and the distinct items seen.
ActionsReport.title: ActionsReport

ApiRecipe-Input.description:
A request and where each field sits in its answer. A learned recipe holds its `proof`; an operator's custom
recipe may hold none: the engineer's test proved it, not held-out pages.
ApiRecipe-Input.title: ApiRecipe

ApiRecipe-Output.description:
A request and where each field sits in its answer. A learned recipe holds its `proof`; an operator's custom
recipe may hold none: the engineer's test proved it, not held-out pages.
ApiRecipe-Output.title: ApiRecipe

Artifact.description:
A stored artifact as an answer names it: the URL the API serves it at, which needs the API's own key like any
other route, and its media type.
Artifact.title: Artifact

AttemptRecord.description: One rung tried. `status` is None when no response arrived (network error, timeout, SSRF rejection).
AttemptRecord.title: AttemptRecord

AttrStep-Input.description: An attribute of the context node: the row in a listing.
AttrStep-Input.title: AttrStep

AttrStep-Output.description: An attribute of the context node: the row in a listing.
AttrStep-Output.title: AttrStep

BatchScrapeRequest-Input.description:
The body of `POST /v1/batch/scrape`. The formats, `schema`, `page_kind`, `fetch` and `locale` are a
scrape's, for every URL. A batch's results are either records or page outputs, so `records` is
asked alone; a `schema.prompt` is not taken (its draft needs a fetched page, which a batch does not wait for),
and `schema.fields` is drafted while the caller waits. Role C fills a page's gaps as in a scrape;
`budget.llm_calls` bounds the job's calls, and without a `budget` the project's cap does, as for every job
kind. The webhook options are `WebhookOptions`.

min_confidence.description: Leave unpublished (abstained) a records field whose calibrated confidence is below this. Unset: every value publishes with its confidence.
min_confidence.title: Min Confidence

render.description: How pages are rendered for fields. `off` (default): HTTP, the browser only when HTTP is refused; a field the HTTP page does not carry is `missing`. `locate`: find where the fields the HTTP pages leave missing (or `fields`) are shown, then fetch each page as they need. `always`: render every page.

BatchScrapeRequest-Input.title: BatchScrapeRequest

BatchScrapeRequest-Output.description:
The body of `POST /v1/batch/scrape`. The formats, `schema`, `page_kind`, `fetch` and `locale` are a
scrape's, for every URL. A batch's results are either records or page outputs, so `records` is
asked alone; a `schema.prompt` is not taken (its draft needs a fetched page, which a batch does not wait for),
and `schema.fields` is drafted while the caller waits. Role C fills a page's gaps as in a scrape;
`budget.llm_calls` bounds the job's calls, and without a `budget` the project's cap does, as for every job
kind. The webhook options are `WebhookOptions`.

min_confidence.description: Leave unpublished (abstained) a records field whose calibrated confidence is below this. Unset: every value publishes with its confidence.
min_confidence.title: Min Confidence

render.description: How pages are rendered for fields. `off` (default): HTTP, the browser only when HTTP is refused; a field the HTTP page does not carry is `missing`. `locate`: find where the fields the HTTP pages leave missing (or `fields`) are shown, then fetch each page as they need. `always`: render every page.

BatchScrapeRequest-Output.title: BatchScrapeRequest

BrowserActions-Input.description:
A single-URL listing scrape's browser actions. `records` is a soft target: the run stops once it
has seen at least that many rows, so it may pass it by one page or batch. Without a `hint` the mechanism is
detected.
BrowserActions-Input.title: BrowserActions

BrowserActions-Output.description:
A single-URL listing scrape's browser actions. `records` is a soft target: the run stops once it
has seen at least that many rows, so it may pass it by one page or batch. Without a `hint` the mechanism is
detected.
BrowserActions-Output.title: BrowserActions

Budget.description:
A request's own bound on its job's LLM calls. A request without one takes the project's `llm_call_cap`, and a
project without a cap bounds none (owner, 2026-10-16; `db.usage.budget_remaining`).
Budget.title: Budget

CallDetail.description:
One call a capture kept (`GET /v1/captures/{id}/calls/{n}`): the request as sent (headers as recorded: no
cookies, the caller's own values masked), the answer's status, headers and text (its UTF-8 decoding, at most
`ANSWER_MAX_BYTES`), the page step it followed and whether it went to the page's own site, and the guard prefix
its JSON opens with.
CallDetail.title: CallDetail

CallList.description:
The calls of the samples, by endpoint in the order they were first called (the samples' order, then each
capture's: its own site's calls first).
CallList.title: CallList

CallRef.description: One call of a sample: its capture and its index among the capture's network bodies.
CallRef.title: CallRef

CallSummary.description:
One call of a sample: its index among the capture's network bodies (`GET /v1/captures/{id}/calls/{n}`), its
answer's status, content type and size, the request's Fetch destination, the page step it followed (0: the page's
load), and whether it went to the page's own site.
CallSummary.title: CallSummary

CallsRequest.description: The sample captures whose calls are merged: two to five, read for one schema, all distinct.
CallsRequest.title: CallsRequest

CaptureRequest.description:
The body of `POST /v1/captures`: a sample page of `schema_id`'s page kind, rendered in the browser after the
page steps (`actions`, `wait_for`, as `fetch` names them), with the caller's `cookies`, through `proxy_pool`.
CaptureRequest.title: CaptureRequest

CaptureResult.description:
An engineer capture: the stored capture (None when nothing was sent: `reason` says why, as a scrape's does),
how its page ended, the records stored from it, and every fetch attempt.
CaptureResult.title: CaptureResult

Chunk.description: One chunk of a page's markdown: its position, text, size in words and the headings above it.
Chunk.title: Chunk

ChunkOptions-Input.description:
`chunks`' options: the `strategy`, the `size` of a chunk and the `overlap` between chunks, in words, and the
markdown the chunks are cut from (`markdown_fit` is pruned, so the chunks hold the page's content only).
ChunkOptions-Input.title: ChunkOptions

ChunkOptions-Output.description:
`chunks`' options: the `strategy`, the `size` of a chunk and the `overlap` between chunks, in words, and the
markdown the chunks are cut from (`markdown_fit` is pruned, so the chunks hold the page's content only).
ChunkOptions-Output.title: ChunkOptions

ClickAction-Input.description: Click an element, or the first visible element whose text holds `text`.
ClickAction-Input.title: ClickAction

ClickAction-Output.description: Click an element, or the first visible element whose text holds `text`.
ClickAction-Output.title: ClickAction

ConfigExport.description: `export` is the IR for `json` and the draft for `platform_draft`; `release` says which fields are `manual`.
ConfigExport.title: ConfigExport

ConfigSummary.description: One version of a site's config for one schema and page kind, without its IR.
ConfigSummary.title: ConfigSummary

ContextHeader.description:
A header the recipe sends with the value the caller's request context holds for `name`: the recipe
stores the name alone, never a value.
ContextHeader.title: ContextHeader

Correction.description:
The body of `PUT /v1/configs/{id}`: steps per field (`null` removes the field), and fields whose steps the
operator confirms.
Correction.title: Correction

CrawlRequest-Input.description:
The body of `POST /v1/crawl`. The formats, `schema`, `fetch` and `locale` are a batch's, for every
    page the crawl extracts: `records` is asked alone, a `schema.prompt` is not taken, and `schema.fields` is
    drafted
    while the caller waits. `budget.llm_calls` bounds the job's LLM calls, and without a `budget` the project's cap
    does.
`include` and `exclude` globs scope the URLs followed, as `map`'s do; `page_kind_rules` decide which
    pages are extracted. The webhook options are `WebhookOptions`.

    `strategy` orders the frontier: `bfs` (breadth first), `dfs` (deepest first) or `best_first`, which leases the
    links that best match `query` and `keywords` first (`crawl.scoring`). `allow_subdomains`
    keeps the start host's subdomains without an `include`, and `allow_external` any host.

limit.description: At most this many pages are fetched.
limit.title: Limit

min_confidence.description: Leave unpublished (abstained) a records field whose calibrated confidence is below this. Unset: every value publishes with its confidence.
min_confidence.title: Min Confidence

render.description: How pages are rendered for fields. `off` (default): HTTP, the browser only when HTTP is refused; a field the HTTP page does not carry is `missing`. `locate`: find where the fields the HTTP pages leave missing (or `fields`) are shown, then fetch each page as they need. `always`: render every page.

CrawlRequest-Input.title: CrawlRequest

CrawlRequest-Output.description:
The body of `POST /v1/crawl`. The formats, `schema`, `fetch` and `locale` are a batch's, for every
    page the crawl extracts: `records` is asked alone, a `schema.prompt` is not taken, and `schema.fields` is
    drafted
    while the caller waits. `budget.llm_calls` bounds the job's LLM calls, and without a `budget` the project's cap
    does.
`include` and `exclude` globs scope the URLs followed, as `map`'s do; `page_kind_rules` decide which
    pages are extracted. The webhook options are `WebhookOptions`.

    `strategy` orders the frontier: `bfs` (breadth first), `dfs` (deepest first) or `best_first`, which leases the
    links that best match `query` and `keywords` first (`crawl.scoring`). `allow_subdomains`
    keeps the start host's subdomains without an `include`, and `allow_external` any host.

limit.description: At most this many pages are fetched.
limit.title: Limit

min_confidence.description: Leave unpublished (abstained) a records field whose calibrated confidence is below this. Unset: every value publishes with its confidence.
min_confidence.title: Min Confidence

render.description: How pages are rendered for fields. `off` (default): HTTP, the browser only when HTTP is refused; a field the HTTP page does not carry is `missing`. `locate`: find where the fields the HTTP pages leave missing (or `fields`) are shown, then fetch each page as they need. `always`: render every page.

CrawlRequest-Output.title: CrawlRequest

CssStep-Input.description: A CSS selector, kept for readability, and its XPath 1.0 translation, which is what executors run.
CssStep-Input.title: CssStep

CssStep-Output.description: A CSS selector, kept for readability, and its XPath 1.0 translation, which is what executors run.
CssStep-Output.title: CssStep

CursorPagination.description: The next request sets `name` to the value the previous response holds at `cursor`, until it holds none.
CursorPagination.title: CursorPagination

CustomRecipe-Input.description:
A custom recipe: the schema and page kind it serves, the URL patterns of one host it serves them for, the main
call and the extra calls by name, the warm-up, the page fields, who sends the calls and the least interval between
them (`rate_ms`).
CustomRecipe-Input.title: CustomRecipe

CustomRecipe-Output.description:
A custom recipe: the schema and page kind it serves, the URL patterns of one host it serves them for, the main
call and the extra calls by name, the warm-up, the page fields, who sends the calls and the least interval between
them (`rate_ms`).
CustomRecipe-Output.title: CustomRecipe

DeliveryOut.description:
One delivery: its status, attempts, when the next one is due (while pending), the last attempt's error and the
status the target answered it with (null before an attempt, or when the target gave none), and how many events it
carries.
DeliveryOut.title: DeliveryOut

DeliveryPage.description:
One page of a job's deliveries, newest first; `next_cursor` is the `cursor` of the page after it, None on the
last.
DeliveryPage.title: DeliveryPage

Delta.description:
What a job's record is against the entity's previous record under the same schema:
`new`, `changed` with its changed fields in schema order, or `same`.
Delta.title: Delta

DeltaCounts.description: How many of a job's records are each delta.
DeltaCounts.title: DeltaCounts

DraftListing.description: `row_xpath` selects the rows (None when the row step is not XPath, and then every row field is `manual`).
DraftListing.title: DraftListing

DroppedRowMeta.description: A row that did not publish: its row entities' locators and the reason.
DroppedRowMeta.title: DroppedRowMeta

Endpoint.description:
One endpoint group: its request method, URL shape (origin, whether there is a path, its segment count, its last
segment's format suffix such as `.json`, "" for none, and the query names in order) and request body shape, the
samples it was called on, its calls, the fields it carries and the row query of the rows it lists.
Endpoint.title: Endpoint

EndpointRef.description: An endpoint of the call list, by its key: request method, URL shape and request body shape (`Endpoint`).
EndpointRef.title: EndpointRef

ExportPage.description: One page of a job's records in an export format; `next_cursor` as in `RecordPage`.
ExportPage.title: ExportPage

ExtractRequest-Input.description:
The body of `POST /v1/extract`. `urls` are URLs and URL globs; `schema` names a schema by id, gives it
inline, or asks for a draft from a `prompt` or from field names (`fields`), and its page kind must
be `page_kind`. `limit` bounds the job's tasks; `budget.llm_calls` (else the project's cap) bounds a prompt's
draft. The `fetch` and `locale` are a scrape's, for every URL. The webhook options are
`WebhookOptions`.

min_confidence.description: Leave unpublished (abstained) a records field whose calibrated confidence is below this. Unset: every value publishes with its confidence.
min_confidence.title: Min Confidence

ExtractRequest-Input.title: ExtractRequest

ExtractRequest-Output.description:
The body of `POST /v1/extract`. `urls` are URLs and URL globs; `schema` names a schema by id, gives it
inline, or asks for a draft from a `prompt` or from field names (`fields`), and its page kind must
be `page_kind`. `limit` bounds the job's tasks; `budget.llm_calls` (else the project's cap) bounds a prompt's
draft. The `fetch` and `locale` are a scrape's, for every URL. The webhook options are
`WebhookOptions`.

min_confidence.description: Leave unpublished (abstained) a records field whose calibrated confidence is below this. Unset: every value publishes with its confidence.
min_confidence.title: Min Confidence

ExtractRequest-Output.title: ExtractRequest

ExtractSubmitted.description: The queued job, and the schema its records are extracted with: a prompt's draft, or the schema named.
ExtractSubmitted.title: ExtractSubmitted

ExtractedRecord.description:
A record's content (§6 `record`): `complete` when every required field and group published, and its
confidence, the minimum over the required fields, `None` when any of them is uncalibrated. A replay answers with
these: they are not stored, so they have no id.
ExtractedRecord.title: ExtractedRecord

FetchOptions-Input.description:
How a request's pages are fetched. `headers` go over HTTP to the page's own host only, never in the browser,
and `cookies` to that host in either; `wait_for` and `actions` run in the browser, so they make the fetch
    a browser one and refuse `method_hint` `http`, and a browser fetch takes no `headers`.
FetchOptions-Input.title: FetchOptions

FetchOptions-Output.description:
How a request's pages are fetched. `headers` go over HTTP to the page's own host only, never in the browser,
and `cookies` to that host in either; `wait_for` and `actions` run in the browser, so they make the fetch
    a browser one and refuse `method_hint` `http`, and a browser fetch takes no `headers`.
FetchOptions-Output.title: FetchOptions

FetchSummary.description:
The fetch of the page: the method, status and class of the kept attempt, the platform adapter that read an `api`
capture (null for any other), and every attempt made.
FetchSummary.title: FetchSummary

FieldChange.description:
A field whose published value differs from the entity's previous record: both values as published, None for a
side that published none.
FieldChange.title: FieldChange

FieldCounts.description: How many fields of a job's records have each status.
FieldCounts.title: FieldCounts

FieldMatch.description:
Where an endpoint carries one schema field: `published` paths read the value a sample published, else `paths`
read a value of the field's type; `in_text` counts the samples whose HTML answer holds the published value's
text.
FieldMatch.title: FieldMatch

FieldReport.description:
One field on the held-out pages. `pages`: held-out pages; `matched`/`valid`: pages where the config matched and
where every match was valid; `published`/`reproduced`: pages where the engine published the field and where both
executors gave that value; `comparable`/`corroborated_on`: pages with a structured or adapter value and where the
config's value equals it. `status` is None for a dropped field, with the check it failed in `dropped`.
FieldReport.title: FieldReport

FieldSpec-Input.description:
One field of a schema, or the item of a list.

The parameters a type needs are present exactly for that type: `vocab` for `enum`, `scheme` for `identifier`,
`item` for `list`, `fields` for `object`. A `list` of `object` with a `schema_org` path is row-mapped (variants):
the path names the row entities, and `key` names the sub-fields that identify a row.
FieldSpec-Input.title: FieldSpec

FieldSpec-Output.description:
One field of a schema, or the item of a list.

The parameters a type needs are present exactly for that type: `vocab` for `enum`, `scheme` for `identifier`,
`item` for `list`, `fields` for `object`. A `list` of `object` with a `schema_org` path is row-mapped (variants):
the path names the row entities, and `key` names the sub-fields that identify a row.
FieldSpec-Output.title: FieldSpec

FieldSteps.description:
A field's steps in order (the first valid value wins), its status, and its held-out yield and validity
once validated.
FieldSteps.title: FieldSteps

FieldType.description: The §5.1 field types. A type is added here only together with its normalizer module (C8).
FieldType.title: FieldType

FieldsDraft.description: Field names and the page kind of the pages they are read from.
FieldsDraft.title: FieldsDraft

FitOptions-Input.description: `markdown_fit`'s options: the `query` the content is kept relevant to, and at most `max_blocks` blocks of it.
FitOptions-Input.title: FitOptions

FitOptions-Output.description: `markdown_fit`'s options: the `query` the content is kept relevant to, and at most `max_blocks` blocks of it.
FitOptions-Output.title: FitOptions

HeaderValue.description: A header the recipe sends with a constant value (`{page_url}` the one placeholder it takes).
HeaderValue.title: HeaderValue

JobCostPage.description:
One page of the jobs with LLM calls in the range, newest first; `next_cursor` is the `cursor` of the page after
it, None on the last.
JobCostPage.title: JobCostPage

JobOutcomes.description: A job's pages by outcome and the fields of its records by status.
JobOutcomes.title: JobOutcomes

JobPage.description: One page of jobs, newest first; `next_cursor` is the `cursor` of the page after it, None on the last.
JobPage.title: JobPage

JsonLdStep-Input.description: A JSONPath into the page's expanded JSON-LD nodes, optionally only those of one schema.org type.
JsonLdStep-Input.title: JsonLdStep

JsonLdStep-Output.description: A JSONPath into the page's expanded JSON-LD nodes, optionally only those of one schema.org type.
JsonLdStep-Output.title: JsonLdStep

JsonValuesItem.description:
A task of a job in `json_values`: its URL, its outcome (null until it ends), the clean records
its page stands for, and, when asked for, its page's metadata and fetch. `records` is empty for a task with no
record (failed, blocked, `links_only`, or a job without a schema). `metadata` is a member only for an extracted or
partial page whose capture is still kept; `fetch` only for a task with a capture that kept its attempts;
`screenshot` and `pdf` with `fetch`, for a capture that kept the file.
JsonValuesItem.title: JsonValuesItem

JsonValuesPage.description:
One page of a job's tasks in `json_values`, oldest first; `next_cursor` is the `cursor` of the page after it,
None on the last.
JsonValuesPage.title: JsonValuesPage

LLMUsage.description:
LLM calls and their tokens, with their estimated cost in USD: null when some of the tokens have no price
(`unpriced_tokens`), never a guess.
LLMUsage.title: LLMUsage

LearnRequest.description: `schema_id` names the schema, and so the page kind, to learn for; `force` re-learns an active one.
LearnRequest.title: LearnRequest

LinkPagination.description:
The next request goes to the target of the previous response's `Link` field with relation type `next`
(RFC 8288 §3), on the recipe's own origin, until it names none.
LinkPagination.title: LinkPagination

ListingReport.description:
`rows_ok`: held-out pages where `row` selected at least `MIN_ROWS` rows; when some page has fewer, the listing is
dropped (`dropped`) and its fields with it.
ListingReport.title: ListingReport

ListingSpec.description:
Rows of a listing page: `row` selects the row nodes, `fields` run relative to each row, `next` locates the next
page's URL. A `jsonpath` row step selects the rows' JSON objects in its source's documents, and its fields' steps
are `jsonpath` steps of the same source read from each row (`$`).
ListingSpec.title: ListingSpec

MapSources.description: How many of the returned URLs came from each source; a URL both found counts as a sitemap's.
MapSources.title: MapSources

ModelRoleUsage.description: The calls to one model for one role (`prompt_kind`).
ModelRoleUsage.title: ModelRoleUsage

NextUrlPagination.description:
The next request goes to the URL the previous response holds at `next` (resolved against the request's URL,
RFC 3986 §5), on the recipe's own origin, until it holds none.
NextUrlPagination.title: NextUrlPagination

NormalizeOp-Input.description: `{"<field type>": {}}`: the type's normalizer runs on the value.
NormalizeOp-Input.title: NormalizeOp

OnePagePagination.description: The listing's one response holds every row `rows` selects: there is no next request.
OnePagePagination.title: OnePagePagination

OutcomeCounts.description: How many of the job's tasks ended with each outcome (`url_task.outcome`).
OutcomeCounts.title: OutcomeCounts

PageField-Input.description:
A field read from the page itself: its steps in order (the first valid value wins), on the HTTP page or, when
only a render states it, the browser's (`browser`).
PageField-Input.title: PageField

PageField-Output.description:
A field read from the page itself: its steps in order (the first valid value wins), on the HTTP page or, when
only a render states it, the browser's (`browser`).
PageField-Output.title: PageField

PageKindRule.description: A crawl's rule: a URL `pattern` matches is extracted as a `page_kind` page.
PageKindRule.title: PageKindRule

PageOutput.description:
A task of a job without a schema, with the content formats the job asked for. The formats
are members only when the task reached its page and its capture is still kept. `last_error` is why the task
failed, or why it ended with its outcome when the outcome alone does not say (a `blocked` task's `robots`), as the
worker recorded it: URLs redacted under `SNOWCRAWL_LOG_REDACT_URLS`.
PageOutput.title: PageOutput

PageOutputPage.description:
One page of a job's tasks, oldest first; `next_cursor` is the `cursor` of the page after it, None on the
last.
PageOutputPage.title: PageOutputPage

ParamPagination.description:
§4.8: the listing's requests set `name` to `start`, `start + step`, ... (a page number or an item offset) until
`rows` selects nothing.
ParamPagination.title: ParamPagination

PathCount.description: A map path, and on how many of the samples a call of the endpoint read it.
PathCount.title: PathCount

Problem.description:
RFC 9457 problem details. `type` is one of the API's problem types, or `about:blank` when the
HTTP status says all there is to say (RFC 9457 §4.2.1); `instance` is the request's path.
Problem.title: Problem

ProjectSettings.description:
`llm_call_cap`: the most LLM calls a job may make when its request sets no `budget.llm_calls`; null: no cap.
`draft_call_cap`: the most uncharged role S calls (field-name drafts) one API key may make, in all; null: no cap.
`require_config_approval`: whether a learned config waits for approval (`POST /v1/configs/{id}/approve`) before it
serves.
ProjectSettings.title: ProjectSettings

Proof.description:
How the recipe was accepted: the held-out captures it reproduced, the headers replay tried and
what bound it.
Proof.title: Proof

Proposal.description:
A custom recipe's draft, with the schema fields its map leaves unfilled, where a value of the request varies
between the samples and nothing binds it (left as the first sample's literal) or looks like a token (left out),
and the captured headers left out (a credential, a token, a value that varies).
Proposal.title: Proposal

ProposeRequest.description: The body of `POST /v1/recipes/propose`: the sample captures, the main call and the schema the recipe serves.
ProposeRequest.title: ProposeRequest

RecipeChange.description:
One part of a recipe a repair changes: its dotted path in the recipe (`main.map.title`, `main.url`,
`calls.stock`), and its value before and after (None where it is not there).
RecipeChange.title: RecipeChange

RecipeFieldReport.description:
One field of an API recipe's map. `published`: held-out pages where the engine published the
field; `reproduced`: those where the replayed response gave that value.
RecipeFieldReport.title: RecipeFieldReport

RecipeReport.description: The API recipe's held-out validation. `refused` says why the recipe did not enter the config.
RecipeReport.title: RecipeReport

RecipeTestRequest.description:
The body of `POST /v1/recipes/test`: the recipe (a draft, or a stored custom recipe's config id), the URLs of
its patterns to try it on, and how they are fetched.
RecipeTestRequest.title: RecipeTestRequest

RecipeTestResult.description: The test's job, each URL's runs in the order asked, and what the job used.
RecipeTestResult.title: RecipeTestResult

RecordPage.description: One page of records, newest first; `next_cursor` is null on the last page.
RecordPage.title: RecordPage

ReleaseField.description:
One field on the held-out pages: `published`, pages where the engine published it; `reproduced`, those where the
release executor gave that value; `manual`, the field failed the check; `executability`, what the field's steps
need to run (`config_ir.executability`).
ReleaseField.title: ReleaseField

ReleaseReport.description:
The release check of one config: the held-out captures it ran on, each field's result, and how many of the
config's fields are in each executability class.
ReleaseReport.title: ReleaseReport

RenderOptions-Input.description:
The `render` member: its mode, and the schema fields `locate` looks for (else the
fields the HTTP extraction left missing). Pinned with the request.
RenderOptions-Input.title: RenderOptions

RenderOptions-Output.description:
The `render` member: its mode, and the schema fields `locate` looks for (else the
fields the HTTP extraction left missing). Pinned with the request.
RenderOptions-Output.title: RenderOptions

RequestBody-Input.description:
A request body with `{name}` placeholders: JSON, where a value is written JSON-escaped (RFC 8259 §7), or
`form`, application/x-www-form-urlencoded (HTML §4.10.21.7), where a value is written percent-encoded.
RequestBody-Input.title: RequestBody

RequestBody-Output.description:
A request body with `{name}` placeholders: JSON, where a value is written JSON-escaped (RFC 8259 §7), or
`form`, application/x-www-form-urlencoded (HTML §4.10.21.7), where a value is written percent-encoded.
RequestBody-Output.title: RequestBody

RowMeta.description: A published row's sub-field outcomes, aligned with the field's value by index.
RowMeta.title: RowMeta

Run.description:
One fetch and extraction of a URL: the records it made, unstored, and its fetch trail (`fetch`, null when
nothing was kept: `reason` says why, as a scrape's does).
Run.title: Run

ScheduleOut.description:
A schedule: its run (`kind`, and `request` as stored, a records schema by id), its cadence, whether it is
paused, when it runs next, and its last run: when, the job it submitted, or why it submitted none.
ScheduleOut.title: ScheduleOut

SchedulePage.description: One page of schedules, newest first; `next_cursor` is the `cursor` of the page after it, None on the last.
SchedulePage.title: SchedulePage

ScheduleUpdate.description:
The members to change; any left out stay. A new `request` comes with its `kind`; a `cron` replaces an interval
and an `interval_s` a cron expression.
ScheduleUpdate.title: ScheduleUpdate

SchemaContent.description: A schema document as a caller writes it, without its name.
SchemaContent.title: SchemaContent

SchemaDef.description:
A `schema_def` row: a document plus where it came from and whether it is in use. One row per
name, edited in place.

`labels` are the synonyms role S drafted for its fields' labels, by field,
editable; None until drafted, and again after an edit of the document. They are no part of the document, so
they change neither its digest nor what was learned for it.
SchemaDef.title: SchemaDef

SchemaFields.description: Field names, drafted into a schema with exactly those top-level fields by role S.
SchemaFields.title: SchemaFields

SchemaLabels.description: The label synonyms of a schema's fields, by field: the labels pages write next to each field's value.
SchemaLabels.title: SchemaLabels

SchemaRef.description:
The schema a config is for: its name, and the digest of its document at learning (`document_digest`). A schema
is edited in place, so only the digest says which document the config was learned for.
SchemaRef.title: SchemaRef

ScrapeRequest-Input.description:
The body of `POST /v1/scrape`. `records` needs a schema and a `page_kind`, and the schema's page kind
must be that one. A `schema.prompt` is drafted and returned, and `budget.llm_calls` (else the project's cap) bounds
its draft; `schema.fields` is drafted before the job, which no budget counts. `max_age` reuses a capture fetched
within that many seconds. `browser_actions` collects more of a listing's rows in the browser; a listing
scrape for `records` in `auto` without it takes the default actions where its page is rendered.

min_confidence.description: Leave unpublished (abstained) a records field whose calibrated confidence is below this. Unset: every value publishes with its confidence.
min_confidence.title: Min Confidence

render.description: How pages are rendered for fields. `off` (default): HTTP, the browser only when HTTP is refused; a field the HTTP page does not carry is `missing`. `locate`: find where the fields the HTTP pages leave missing (or `fields`) are shown, then fetch each page as they need. `always`: render every page.

ScrapeRequest-Input.title: ScrapeRequest

ScrapeRequest-Output.description:
The body of `POST /v1/scrape`. `records` needs a schema and a `page_kind`, and the schema's page kind
must be that one. A `schema.prompt` is drafted and returned, and `budget.llm_calls` (else the project's cap) bounds
its draft; `schema.fields` is drafted before the job, which no budget counts. `max_age` reuses a capture fetched
within that many seconds. `browser_actions` collects more of a listing's rows in the browser; a listing
scrape for `records` in `auto` without it takes the default actions where its page is rendered.

min_confidence.description: Leave unpublished (abstained) a records field whose calibrated confidence is below this. Unset: every value publishes with its confidence.
min_confidence.title: Min Confidence

render.description: How pages are rendered for fields. `off` (default): HTTP, the browser only when HTTP is refused; a field the HTTP page does not carry is `missing`. `locate`: find where the fields the HTTP pages leave missing (or `fields`) are shown, then fetch each page as they need. `always`: render every page.

ScrapeRequest-Output.title: ScrapeRequest

ScrapeResult.description:
The answer to a scrape. A page that robots.txt kept from being fetched has no capture, so
`capture_id`, `final_url`, `fetched_at` and `fetch` are None, and `reason` says why, as the task's `last_error`
does: `robots` for a disallow, `robots_unreachable` for a robots.txt that could not be read (RFC
9309 §2.3.1.4), `slow_down` for a host whose turn at its rate was more than a minute off; for a fetched page a
vendor's challenge kept out, `challenge: <vendor>`; for a fetched listing whose extraction gave no rows,
`no_rows: <cause>` (`no_rows` in `resolve.pipeline`, "Scrape outcomes, not errors, for page
failures"); None for any other page that was fetched. `schema` is the draft of a `schema.prompt`.
ScrapeResult.title: ScrapeResult

ScrapedRecord.description: A stored record as `scrape` answers with it.
ScrapedRecord.title: ScrapedRecord

ScrollAction-Input.description: Scroll to the end (`to: bottom`), by `by` CSS pixels, or until the document stops growing (`until: stable`).
ScrollAction-Input.title: ScrollAction

ScrollAction-Output.description: Scroll to the end (`to: bottom`), by `by` CSS pixels, or until the document stops growing (`until: stable`).
ScrollAction-Output.title: ScrollAction

SearchRequest.description: The body of `POST /v1/search`: `query`, at most `limit` results, and optionally how to `scrape` them.
SearchRequest.title: SearchRequest

job_id.description: The batch job scraping the results, with `scrape`
job_id.title: Job Id

skipped.description: Results the API may not fetch, left out of the scrape
skipped.title: Skipped

SearchScrape.description:
How the results are scraped: a batch's `formats` (markdown when none), `schema`, `page_kind`, `fetch`,
`locale`, `budget` and `webhook_url`, for every result (`BatchScrapeRequest`).
SearchScrape.title: SearchScrape

StoredRecord.description:
A `record` row, with the capture it was extracted from (`None` once the capture expired),
the schema its fields follow, its own version and the fields whose published value differs from the
version it supersedes, empty for an entity's first. `egress_country` is the ISO 3166-1 country the
page was fetched from (null: unknown) and `egress_basis` how that is known: `pool` (the proxy pool's declared
country), `machine` (a direct fetch from the machine's declared country) or `unknown`.
StoredRecord.title: StoredRecord

SubFieldMeta.description: A row sub-field's outcome without its candidates.
SubFieldMeta.title: SubFieldMeta

TaskCounts.description: How many of the job's tasks are in each status.
TaskCounts.title: TaskCounts

TypeAction-Input.description: Type `text` into an element; refused in the browser for a password or credential field.
TypeAction-Input.title: TypeAction

TypeAction-Output.description: Type `text` into an element; refused in the browser for a password or credential field.
TypeAction-Output.title: TypeAction

UrlTest.description: A URL tried: with the recipe, and with the normal extraction.
UrlTest.title: UrlTest

ValidationReport.description:
The `extraction_config.validation_report`. `refused` says why nothing can activate;
`api_recipe` is the recipe's validation when the site has one.
ValidationReport.title: ValidationReport

WaitAction-Input.description: Wait `ms` milliseconds, for an element to be visible, or for the network to be idle (`network_idle`).
WaitAction-Input.title: WaitAction

WaitAction-Output.description: Wait `ms` milliseconds, for an element to be visible, or for the network to be idle (`network_idle`).
WaitAction-Output.title: WaitAction

WarmUp-Input.description:
The request a custom recipe's calls follow: the page itself (`url` null), or a fixed URL whose `{name}`
placeholders are the URL pattern's parameters. Its answer may bind the calls' parameters (`warm_up*` binders).
WarmUp-Input.title: WarmUp

WarmUp-Output.description:
The request a custom recipe's calls follow: the page itself (`url` null), or a fixed URL whose `{name}`
placeholders are the URL pattern's parameters. Its answer may bind the calls' parameters (`warm_up*` binders).
WarmUp-Output.title: WarmUp

WebhookBatch.description:
How a job's webhook events are grouped: up to `max_events` a delivery, sent when that many wait or the oldest
has waited `max_seconds`, whichever comes first.
WebhookBatch.title: WebhookBatch

post.description:
Render `url` in the browser after the page steps, keeping every call the page makes, and store the capture and
its record of the schema: a sample page to choose a custom recipe's calls from. Answers when the page has been
fetched and read, as `POST /v1/scrape` does, with its problems.

get.description:
The screenshot (`screenshot.png`) or PDF (`page.pdf`) the browser made of the capture's page, as the scrape,
batch or crawl that asked for it named it in its answer. 404: no such capture, its files expired with it, or it has
no such file.

200.description: The file: a PNG for `screenshot.png`, a PDF for `page.pdf`.

get.description:
The capture's calls by endpoint, each with where it carries the fields of the schema it was read for (the values
of its record, else the paths of each field's type). 404: no such capture, or its bundle expired; 409: it was read
for no schema.

The capture as an HTTP Archive (HAR 1.2): the page's document and every call it kept, without cookies, the
caller's own header values masked. 404: no such capture, or its bundle expired.

One call the capture kept, by its index in the call list: the request and the answer's text. 404: no such
capture or call, or its bundle expired.

post.description:
The records the current engine makes from the capture, against the schemas of the records stored from
it. 404: no such capture, or its bundle expired; 409: no record was made from it.

get.description: The config's IR and validation report.

put.description:
Corrects or confirms fields (C5): the next version, `origin=operator`, validated on the site's held-out pages.
It is `active` when validation keeps a field, else `draft`; its validation report says why. `config_id` must be
the latest version of its site, schema and page kind; otherwise 409.

post.description:
Approves a learned config waiting as `pending_approval` (the project's `require_config_approval`): it becomes the
active config of its site, schema and page kind, and the version active before is `suspended`. 409 for a config
in any other status.

The config as `json` (the IR as stored) or `platform_draft` (`draft: true` until the platform's format is known),
and the release check on the pages the config was validated on: a field the independent release executor does not
reproduce on every such page with an engine value while there are fewer than 10, or on 95% from 10 on, is
`manual`.

put.description:
Edits a custom recipe: the next version, `active`, replacing `config_id`, which is `suspended`. 409 when
`config_id` is not a custom recipe or not the latest version of its patterns' shape, or when another active recipe
serves a pattern of a new shape.

post.description:
Refuses a learned config waiting as `pending_approval`: it becomes `suspended`, the version active before goes on
serving, and the site learns again only after 8 more extracted pages. 409 for a config in any other status or not
the latest version.

Queue a job that crawls from `url`: its sitemaps and the links of each page, within `include` and `exclude`,
`max_depth` and `limit`, on its host (and the subdomains an `include` names). A page a `page_kind_rules` pattern
matches is extracted; with rules, any other page is fetched for its links only. `strategy` orders the visits: `bfs`
(default), `dfs`, or `best_first`, which fetches the links that best match `query` and `keywords` first (anchor
text and URL path against the query, the holding page's relevance, sitemap priority, shallower first);
`allow_subdomains` and `allow_external` widen the host scope. Pages the `limit` leaves unfetched end `cancelled`.
A target the API may not fetch, in `url` or `webhook_url`, is a 422 and nothing is queued.

Queue a job that extracts a record of `page_kind` from each of `urls`; a URL with a `*` is a glob, expanded
through a map of its host. A `schema.prompt` is drafted from the first pages before the job is queued, and the
draft is returned as `schema`. A target the API may not fetch, a URL by its form, a glob's origin or map or
`webhook_url`, is a 422 and nothing is queued; a URL refused only once its host is resolved (`dns`, a private
address) fails its own task.

get.description:
The jobs, newest first, each with the summary `GET /v1/jobs/{id}` answers; only those of `kind` and `status`
when given. Pass a page's `next_cursor` as `cursor` for the page after it.

delete.description:
Cancel the job: its queued tasks are not run, and it is `cancelled` once no task is running. 409: it already
completed or failed.

get.description: The job's status, its task counts by status and by outcome, and its usage.

The job's run events in the order they were stored, each with its id, then a `progress` event with the task
counts after each batch, until the event of the job's end (`completed`, `failed` or `cancelled`), after which
the stream closes. Send the last id received as `Last-Event-ID` to resume after it.

The job's pages as an `llms-full.txt`: the opening of `llms.txt`, then each page's Markdown under its title, up
to 1000 pages. 409: no page.

The job's pages as an `llms.txt` (llmstxt.org): the site's name and summary from its first page, then links to
the pages it reached, each with its title and description, in sections by the first segment of their paths. Made
from the captures, for any job that reached pages (a crawl, batch or extract), up to 5000 pages. 409: no page.

The job's pages by outcome, and the fields of its records by status with the reasons the unpublished ones give:
counted from what the job stored.

The request the job was submitted with, with its `kind`: the kind's request model as the server validated and
stored it (defaults filled in, `fetch` header and cookie values redacted). 404 for a `learn` job, which the system
starts without one.

schema.title: Response Get Job Request V1 Jobs  Job Id  Request Get

get.description:
The job's records, newest first: in the field shape of `/v1/records` (`format=json`), or as `json_records`,
`csv_records`, `markdown` or `jsonl` (JSON Lines) text in the schema's columns, or all of them as one file,
`xlsx` (Excel) or `parquet` (Apache Parquet, 503 `format_unavailable` where pyarrow is not installed), which take no
`cursor` or `limit`. A job without a schema answers `format=json` with its
tasks, oldest first, each with the content formats the job asked for once its page was reached, and its fetch (the
attempts made, as a scrape answers them). Any job
answers `format=json_values` with its tasks, oldest first, each with its URL, outcome and clean records (the
schema's fields in name order, each its published value or null); `include=metadata`, accepted with `json_values`
only, adds a reached page's metadata while its capture is kept, and `include=fetch` its fetch. `csv_safe=true`,
accepted with `csv_records` only, prefixes `'` to each cell starting with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, a tab or a carriage
return, so a spreadsheet shows it as text (OWASP CSV Injection); without it the export is the published values
unchanged. Pass a page's `next_cursor` as `cursor` for the page after it. 409: an export other than `json_values`
of a job without a schema.

schema.title: Response Job Results V1 Jobs  Job Id  Results Get

get.description:
The job's webhook deliveries, newest first, for debugging a receiver: each one's status (`pending`, `delivered`
or `failed`), attempts, the last attempt's error and the HTTP status the target answered with, and how many events
it carries. Ended deliveries are kept 30 days. Pass a page's `next_cursor` as `cursor` for the page after it.

post.description:
The URLs of `url`'s site from its sitemaps and the start page's links, canonical and in scope: the exact host
of `url`, or the `include` globs, less the `exclude` globs. At most `limit`; `truncated` says more were found, or
that reading stopped at a cap or the 60 s timeout.

get.description:
The project's settings. `llm_call_cap` bounds the LLM calls of every job whose request sets no
`budget.llm_calls`, and `draft_call_cap` the uncharged field-name drafts of each API key; null bounds none.
`require_config_approval` makes a learned config wait for approval before it serves.

patch.description:
Set the project's settings. A new `llm_call_cap` applies to running jobs too, from their next LLM call, and a new
`draft_call_cap` from a key's next draft; `require_config_approval` from the next learning run's end.

post.description:
The samples' calls by endpoint, each field's paths counted on how many samples they read it. 404: no such
capture, or its bundle expired; 409: a capture was read for no schema, or they were read for different ones.

A custom recipe's draft from the samples' calls of the `main` endpoint (named by its key or one of its calls),
for the schema: the bound request, its headers, pagination, field map and URL patterns, with the fields left
unfilled, the request values left unbound and the headers left out. Deterministic, and nothing is sent or stored.
404: no such capture or schema, or a bundle expired; 422: the samples' calls of the main endpoint make no recipe.

Each URL fetched and extracted with the recipe (a draft, or a stored custom recipe's id), and as if no recipe's
pattern matched it, both with their fetch trails. No capture, record, config or site memory is stored; the
fetches count as a `scrape` job's usage. 404: no such config or schema; 409: the config is not a custom recipe;
422: the draft does not fit its schema, or a URL matches no pattern of the recipe.

get.description:
Records newest first, narrowed by job, site (host) and schema. Pass a page's `next_cursor` as `cursor`
for the page after it.
The schedules, newest first. Pass a page's `next_cursor` as `cursor` for the page after it.

post.description:
Store a recurring run of `request` (of `kind`: a scrape runs as the batch of its URL), at each time of the
5-field `cron` expression in `timezone`, or every `interval_s` seconds (at least 60). The request is checked as
its submission would be (targets, schema); a `records` schema is stored by id. Its jobs are submitted as this key's,
which signs their webhooks.

delete.description: Delete the schedule. Its jobs stay, with `schedule_id` null.

patch.description:
Change the schedule's name, cadence, or run (`kind` with `request`, checked as at creation); a changed cadence
is due at its first time after now.

post.description: Stop the schedule's runs until it is resumed.
Run the schedule again from its first due time after now; the runs missed while paused are not made up.
Submit the schedule's job now, paused or not; its next due time stays as it is.

get.description: Every schema, by name; only `name` and those in `status` when given.

post.description: A new `user` schema.

The schema role S drafts from `fields` for `page_kind` pages, with exactly those top-level fields, as a run's
`schema.fields` uses it: the stored draft when these names were drafted for this page kind before, else a new
one, stored. A client shows it for editing before the run. A draft the LLM could not give is a
problem typed with the LLM failure (502, 503), or a 429 once the key has made the project's `draft_call_cap` of
them; a retired draft is a 422.

delete.description: Retires the schema. The row stays, since records and configs reference it; a preset is refused (409).

put.description:
Replaces the schema's document with `body`, in place, and returns it. Its active site configs are suspended
and its sites learn again. A retired schema or a preset is refused (409).

Replaces the schema's label synonyms (drafted by role S on its first use) with `body`, and returns it. They are
no part of its document, so nothing is learned again; a preset's can be edited too. A retired schema is refused
(409).

post.description:
Fetch `url`, or read a capture of it fetched within `max_age` seconds, and return the requested formats; only
those are members of the answer. A `schema.prompt` is drafted into a schema, returned as `schema`. `records`
holds the page's record against the schema; an inline schema is stored as a `user` schema, or matched to the
stored schema of its name, and one that differs from it is a 409.

The web results of `query` from the configured provider: `url`, `title` and `snippet`, in its order, at most
`limit`. With `scrape`, a batch job scrapes the results (`job_id`); a result the API may not fetch is counted in
`skipped`. 503 `search_unavailable` when no provider is configured, 502 when the provider does not answer.

get.description:
Every version of the site's configs, custom recipes included, with status, field status and validation report,
by schema, page kind and version.

post.description:
Saves a custom recipe: the site's next config version for the schema and page kind, `origin=operator`,
`active` at once. It serves the URLs its patterns match; the learned config stays active and serves the rest.
409 when an active recipe of the site, schema and page kind already serves a URL pattern of the same shape (the
pattern with its parameter names left out); 422 when the recipe does not fit the site or schema.

Starts learning the site's config for a schema; 409 while a run is in flight, or when the site has an
active config and `force` is not set.

get.description:
The LLM calls of the UTC days `start` to `end` (both included; by default the 30 days through today), with
their tokens and estimated cost in USD: in total, per day, per provider, model and prompt kind, and for the
costliest jobs. A cost is null when some of its tokens have no price. Calls made without a job are not
recorded, so they are not included.

The jobs with LLM calls in the range, newest first, each with those calls' tokens and estimated cost. Pass a
page's `next_cursor` as `cursor` for the page after it.
